newsitem.title: GERMANY: SPD says tax talks depend on new Kohl proposals.
newsitem.headline: SPD says tax talks depend on new Kohl proposals.

text.p: Oskar Lafontaine, head of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), said again on Thursday Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition would have to come up with new proposals on tax reform if the SPD is to return to the bargaining table.
"I am ready if Chancellor Kohl wants to discuss new proposals with me," Lafontaine said in a statement.
SPD says tax talks depend on new Kohl proposals

"The government's proposals up to now are no contribution to the fight against unemployment," Lafontaine said. The government's plan is lacking 44 billion marks in financing, and is not a serious basis for negotiations, he said.
Kohl must make proposals that will cut taxes as of January 1998 and reduce the burden of other withholdings from wages such as social security paynments, Lafontaine said.
The SPD boycotted a round of tax reform talks slated for last Saturday in protest against the government's plans to curtail subsidies for domestic coal mining.
SPD officials said this week, however, their return to tax talks was not dependent on a resolution of the coal crisis.
After a deal on the coal subsidies was announced earlier on Thursday, Kohl's Christian Democrats urged the SPD to return to the tax talks, saying there was now no obstacle.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel says his tax reform plan, including 30 billion marks in net tax cuts, will boost jobs and investment. It is slated to start in 1999, though the government has said some parts could be moved up to next year.
